content.text:
Hi Avichal Dwivedi,

Your team Cue has completed web check-in. You’re ready to build!

As team leader, you receive the setup and credits instructions for your team. Credits are allocated once per team, not per member.

## Join the neatHack Discord

Join our Discord for event announcements, help with setup and credits, and support from organisers and mentors.

[https://neatlogs.com/discord](https://neatlogs.com/discord)

## 1. Build with neatlogs — free throughout the hackathon

All neatlogs paid plans are available to you for free for the duration of neatHack. We believe no good idea should be held back by a paywall.

Sign up at [https://app.neatlogs.com](https://app.neatlogs.com) and create your project.

Start with our step-by-step setup guide, with screenshots, a ready-to-use coding-agent prompt, and troubleshooting: [https://neatlogs.com/hackathon/neatlogs-setup-guide.html](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon/neatlogs-setup-guide.html)

For framework-specific instructions, see [https://docs.neatlogs.com.](https://docs.neatlogs.com)

Run your agent and verify that its traces appear in the dashboard. Use those traces to investigate failures and verify your fixes.

## 2. Set up Entire

Follow the Entire guide for neatHack: [https://hack.entire.io/neathacks-2026/](https://hack.entire.io/neathacks-2026/)

Connect your GitHub repository, install the CLI, and capture your first checkpoint.

Explore Trails and optional Graph/Brain features. Include an accessible checkpoint link and ID in your submission.

## 3. Access [cfo.ai](http://cfo.ai/) paid plans for free

Use the dedicated neatHack signup link to access any [cfo.ai](http://cfo.ai/) paid plan for free: [https://cfo.ai/neathacks](https://cfo.ai/neathacks)

A card is required during signup. Immediately after signing up, cancel your subscription in Settings → Billing. You won’t be billed if you cancel immediately.

The neatHack team will provide your [cfo.ai](http://cfo.ai/) credits directly.

Use [cfo.ai](http://cfo.ai/) to plan your agent’s pricing, costs, revenue, and runway. Include the resulting business plan in your submission.

## 4. Claim your Crustdata credits

Get 5,000 Crustdata credits to build with company and people data.

Use promo code: NEATLOGS-OCT2026

Open [https://app.crustdata.com](https://app.crustdata.com) and select “Have a promo code?” below Continue. Add the code before signing up with your email. Use email signup, not “Continue with Google”, so the code can be applied. Already have an account, or need help? Contact the neatHack organisers at [https://neatlogs.com/discord.](https://neatlogs.com/discord)

API documentation: [https://www.crustdata.com/api-documentation](https://www.crustdata.com/api-documentation)

## Before you build

Every project must use neatlogs, Entire, and [cfo.ai](http://cfo.ai/). Keep evidence of all three for your submission and demo.

Hackathon guide: [https://neatlogs.com/hackathon](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon)

Build-log skill: [https://neatlogs.com/hackathon/skill](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon/skill)

View your team: [https://neatlogs.com/hackathon/check-in](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon/check-in)

Get help on Discord: [https://neatlogs.com/discord](https://neatlogs.com/discord)

See you at neatHack!

The neatlogs team

content.text:
**Yes—Cue fits this track well. I’d keep the core idea.** Its customer report → investigation → code change → independent tests → human approval → verified resolution workflow directly matches what they’re asking for.

After inspecting the code and verification records, I’d prioritize these changes:

1. **Complete the required sponsor integrations.** I couldn’t find neatlogs instrumentation, accessible Entire checkpoint evidence, or a cfo.ai business plan in the checked-in project. These are mandatory, and effective sponsor use carries **25% of the score**. [Official criteria](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon)

2. **Make one complete workflow the main demo.** Show a customer reporting a Bloom problem, Cue investigating and producing a tested fix, then the approval and verified outcome. Explain where humans approve consequential actions.

3. **Show failure and recovery.** Capture a failed run and an improved run in neatlogs, with the same task and a measurable difference. That demonstrates why Cue is useful beyond its interface.

4. **Prepare a public submission repository.** I verified that `cue-b2c` is currently private; they require public code and a demo of three minutes or less. [Submission requirements](https://neatlogs.com/hackathon)

Growth can be a supporting example. Its recorded journey proves a controlled activation, but organic acquisition remains unproven—keep the sample metrics clearly labelled. [Verification report](/Users/avichaldwivedi/dev/Cue/cue-demo/docs/REDACTED.md:23)

**My recommendation: finish the sponsor evidence and prove one fresh end-to-end run before expanding Cue further.**

+# Cue business plan — neatHack 2026
+
+Cue helps small consumer-app teams turn customer reports into investigated,
+reviewed, and verified product changes. The first customer is a founder or a
+small product team maintaining one app and receiving repeated support reports.
+Bloom is our controlled demonstration app, not a paying customer.
+
+## Offer and pricing hypothesis
+
+Test a $99/month plan for one app: 50 support conversations and five scoped
+coding investigations, with human approval before publishing or releasing.
+This is a proposed pilot price, not a launched plan or willingness-to-pay result.
+Start with three to five design partners. Retain manual review for uncertain
+grouping and limit coding to a connected, trusted repository and approved paths.
+
+## Cost model
+
+All dollar amounts below are planning allowances, not measured provider bills.
+Assume $0.02 per support conversation, $3 per coding investigation, $3 variable
+infrastructure per customer, and $75/month fixed hosting/observability/tools.
+Variable cost is therefore $19/customer/month. Cost of a coding investigation
+is the biggest unmeasured expense; capture real usage before selling a quota.
+
+| Paying customers | Revenue/month | Cost/month | Contribution/month | Margin |
+|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
+| 0 | $0 | $75 | -$75 | — |
+| 1 | $99 | $94 | $5 | 5.1% |
+| 5 | $495 | $170 | $325 | 65.7% |
+| 20 | $1,980 | $455 | $1,525 | 77.0% |
+
+Formula: revenue = customers × 99; cost = 75 + customers × 19.
+Founder salary, taxes, payment fees, sales effort, and refunds are excluded;
+these are contribution margins, not net profit. Hackathon credits are excluded
+from steady-state economics. With a hypothetical $1,000 cash budget and zero
+revenue, infrastructure-only runway is 13.3 months at $75/month. Cash and funding
+have not been supplied, so this is a scenario rather than actual runway.
+
+Stress case: at $12 per investigation, variable cost becomes $64/customer.
+At 20 customers, contribution drops to $625/month and margin to 31.6%.
+Fallback: charge expensive coding runs separately, reduce the included quota,
+or provide investigation-only workflows until costs are predictable.
+
+## Smallest falsifiable pilot
+
+Recruit three founders with a trusted app repository. Over one week, compare
+ten eligible support reports per founder with their current manual workflow.
+Match report complexity and record elapsed human work, coding/provider cost,
+independent acceptance checks, rejected suggestions, and required edits.
+Keep a separate set of unseen reports for final assessment.
+
+Success: at least 30% less human work on eligible reports, zero cross-app data
+exposure or unsupported release claims, independent checks passing before
+resolution, and at least two founders agreeing to the $99 paid pilot.
+Stop automatic grouping on any false merge. Stop autonomous implementation on
+any protected-file change or approval bypass. Pivot to support investigation
+and draft preparation if median human savings are below 20%, or if fewer than
+two founders want to pay. Add complexity only after this baseline succeeds.
+
+## Current evidence and limits
+
+The inspected application retains a real scoped Codex investigation, protected
+tests, a reviewed commit, and deployed acceptance evidence. A fresh replay of
+the upload fixture produces three failed acceptance checks before the limit
+fix and eight passing HTTP checks afterward. This replay applies the existing
+one-line correction in a temporary copy; it is not a new autonomous coding run.
+Fresh Gemini support, classification, specification, and Growth calls have
+neatlogs traces. Their controlled drafts were not sent to customers.
+
+Growth has a previously verified controlled publication-to-Bloom activation
+journey. Organic acquisition, retention, paid customers, and revenue are
+unmeasured. Generic arbitrary-repository bug fixing and unattended releases
+are outside the demonstrated scope.
+
+## cfo.ai evidence
+
+Account email is verified. Workspace access awaits the user completing the
+trial/card step and immediately canceling the subscription, as instructed in
+the event email. This document is the prepared model input. It must not be
+represented as a cfo.ai-generated plan until the actual workspace model and

readme='''# Cue · neatHack 2026

Cue helps consumer-app teams turn customer feedback into investigated, reviewed and independently verified product changes. Bloom is the reference photo-journal app.

- [Cue](https://cue.latchgrid.in) · [operator workspace](https://cue.latchgrid.in/cue#/home) (sign-in and team membership required)
- [Bloom customer app](https://bloom-with-cue.vercel.app)
- [Business plan](docs/neathack-business-plan.md) · [Demo script](docs/neathack-demo-script.md) · [Submission evidence](docs/neathack-submission.md)

## What works

Support reports are saved, classified and linked to issues. Cue can run a scoped Codex investigation against its Bloom fixture, keep independent tests outside the editable surface, and require human approval of the exact patch before release. App-bound feature repositories have a separate trusted execution path. Arbitrary repositories and arbitrary bug deployment are outside this demo's supported scope.

The retained upload run has a real coding session, independently checked patch and approved release. Fresh neatlogs evidence includes actual Gemini support/triage/specification/Growth calls and a temporary-copy replay of the upload regression. The replay applies the known correction; it is not a new autonomous coding run. Growth activation evidence is controlled; no organic acquisition or paying customers are claimed.

## Run locally
